Horsehead + Flame Nebula plan, Feb 10, 35°N:
Both objects are in Orion, near Alnitak (Zeta Orionis). At 480mm focal length (80mm f/6), the field of view is roughly 3x2 degrees — sufficient to frame both.
Framing: Center on Alnitak, Horsehead is just south, Flame is adjacent. Rotate camera so both fit along the long axis of the sensor.
Exposure settings: ISO 800-1600, individual exposures 120-180 seconds (with autoguiding). Total integration: 2-3 hours minimum (40-60 subs at 180s). Take 20 darks, 30 flats, 30 bias frames.
Schedule: Start after astronomical twilight (~7pm), image until target sets in west (~1-2am). New moon = no interference. Best when target is highest (transit ~10pm).

Perseid Star Party plan, August 12, 9pm-1am:
9:00-9:30pm: Welcome and safety briefing. Use laser pointer to show Summer Triangle (Vega, Deneb, Altair). Point out Perseus rising in northeast. Discuss what meteors are.
9:30-10:00pm: Binocular tour of Milky Way from Sagittarius to Cygnus. Show M8 (Lagoon Nebula), M13 (Hercules Cluster). Meteors may be visible already.
10:00-10:30pm: Telescope targets - Saturn (rings visible, crowd favorite), then Albireo (double star, gold and blue, easy split in any telescope).
10:30-11:00pm: Break/activity - constellation identification challenge, Q&A while sky clears.
11:00pm-12:00am: Peak meteor watching. Lie-back viewing with blankets. Telescope on M57 (Ring Nebula) and M27 (Dumbbell Nebula) for interested viewers. Count meteors per 15-min interval.
12:00-1:00am: Late targets - Andromeda Galaxy M31 (rising east), Double Cluster in Perseus. Final meteor count tally. Wrap up with astrophotography tips for smartphone through eyepiece.

items.answer:
Variable star campaign, Sep-Nov, 6-inch reflector + CCD:
1. Delta Cephei (Cepheid variable, mag 3.5-4.4, period 5.37 days): Founding member of Cepheid distance ladder. Observe every 2-3 nights to trace full light curve. Bright enough for visual estimates too.
2. Algol / Beta Persei (eclipsing binary, mag 2.1-3.4, period 2.87 days): Eclipses last ~10 hours, observe during predicted minima (check AAVSO predictions). Scientifically valuable for orbital period studies.
3. R Leonis (Mira variable, mag 4.4-11.3, period 310 days): Long-period pulsating giant. Observe weekly. Rising toward maximum in this period. Contributes to mass-loss studies in late-stage stellar evolution.
4. SS Cygni (dwarf nova, mag 7.7-12.1, outbursts every ~50 days): Cataclysmic variable with unpredictable outbursts. Observe every clear night to catch outbursts. Data helps understand accretion disk physics.
5. W Ursae Majoris (W UMa type eclipsing binary, mag 7.8-8.5, period 0.33 days): Contact binary with rapid period. Observe 2-3 times per week. Period changes indicate mass transfer and angular momentum loss.
Schedule: Priority observations during predicted Algol minima and when SS Cygni is near expected outburst. Regular cadence for Delta Cephei and W UMa. Weekly check on R Leonis. Report all data to AAVSO via WebObs.
